gen-dafont-dogica-gf-noto-sans-cherokee: Heavy and wide-spaced, Dogica stamps its headings with lowercase that nearly reaches the capitals. Noto Sans Cherokee settles underneath with a tall band of letters and an e left gaping at its terminal, friendly where the top is blunt.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-noto-sans-chorasmia: Commanding in its wide tracking and near-capital lowercase, Dogica makes every heading land hard and clear. Noto Sans Chorasmian does the quieter job of big, readable text.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-noto-sans-coptic: Blocky, stretched out and loud, Dogica leaves a gap at the end of every curve in its headings. Noto Sans Coptic keeps to a tidy middle zone beneath.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-noto-sans-cuneiform: Dogica's lowercase climbs almost to the height of its capitals, then spreads out on very wide tracking. Noto Sans Cuneiform follows with e shapes that open up and puffed-out letters like inflated glass beads, so text feels round and buoyant.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-noto-sans-deseret: Commanding from the first letter, Dogica sets heavy, widely tracked headings above the text. And Noto Sans Deseret answers with squat ascenders and open apertures, giving the page a softer, easier floor.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-noto-sans-devanagar: Noto Sans Devanagari reads compactly, its capitals melting into the lowercase and its g curling open at the bottom. And Dogica supplies the muscle, heavy and widely spaced, which is what makes the two so different.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-noto-sans-duployan: Chunky, stretched and unmistakably loud, Dogica heads the page with curves that never quite close. Noto Sans Duployan sits next to it with a wide-mouthed a and oversized counters, friendlier and roomier than the heading.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-noto-sans-elbasan: Commanding and heavy, Dogica pushes its near-capital lowercase out on very wide tracking, while Noto Sans Elbasan brings large forms and terminals that never pinch. Heavy up top, open below.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-noto-sans-elymaic: Loud, wide and blocky, Dogica is built for heading impact with its heavy, spread-out lowercase. But Noto Sans Elymaic does the gentler work, with open apertures and low ascenders for steady text.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-noto-sans-ethiopic: Big, blunt and widely spaced, Dogica hits hard with near-capital lowercase. Noto Sans Ethiopic is the sturdy reader, with tall letters and c terminals hanging far from the bowl.
